body:
---
guardian_issue:
  id: "ISSUE-TEN-DOCTESTS-ARE-IGNORED_ON_PUBLIC_APIS"
  title: "10 of rigorix_engine's 16 doctests are `ignore` — including the example for `with_pinned_inputs`, the documented way to use ADR-014's carrier — so they never compile"
  epic: "portable-slice"
  component: "Engine"
  module: "wasm-seam"
  status: planned
  priority: medium
  tracking_issue: 1379
  dependencies:
    - "#1373 (introduced the doctest floor over *executed* examples)"

  intent: |
    `bash .pi/scripts/run-doctests.sh` reports `rigorix_engine 16 discovered 6 executed 10 ignored`,
    and the floor in `.pi/doctest-floors.tsv` ratchets the *executed* count at 6 for exactly this
    reason: `cargo test --doc` prints "running 16 tests" and then runs six.

    An `ignore` fence is not a slow example; it is an example that is **never compiled**. So the ten
    are documentation that cannot be wrong in public, which is the one property a doc example is for.
    Among them:

    ```
    engine/src/audit/application/envelope_factory_impl.rs:69   AuditEnvelopeFactoryImpl::with_pinned_inputs
    engine/src/configuration/domain/secret.rs:31               Secret
    engine/src/recovery_recipes/application/context.rs:25      RecoveryContext
    engine/src/tools/infrastructure/tree_sitter_anchor.rs:36   AnchorParams
    engine/src/budget_tracking/application/service.rs:106      LlmBudgetReservation…
    engine/src/failure_classification/application/classify.rs  classify
    ```

    The first is the sharpest: `with_pinned_inputs` is the method ADR-014 §2 introduced as the way to
    supply a pinned instant, its usage example is `ignore`, and nothing compiles it. The engine's
    public surface documents the decision's carrier with a snippet that has never been built.

    #1373 recorded the gap and named it as worth an issue; it was not filed, so the floor records a
    number without an owner for it.

  in_scope:
    - "Every `ignore` fence on a public API is converted to a compiling example: a plain fence when it can run, `no_run` when it needs a network, a database or a filesystem, and `ignore` only with a stated reason recorded in `.pi/doctest-exemptions.tsv` (path, item, why)"
    - "The floor in `.pi/doctest-floors.tsv` is raised to the new executed count, so the conversions cannot be undone silently"
    - "`with_pinned_inputs`'s example compiles and, if it can run without a key, runs"

  out_of_scope:
    - "Adding examples to items that have none. This is about examples that exist and do not compile"
    - "A doctest for every public item — the floor is a ratchet, not a target"
    - "The `run-doctests.sh` mechanics, which work: floors, per-crate reporting, and a failure that names the crate"

  affected_layers:
    domain:
      - "Documentation examples on public domain types (`Secret`, `AnchorParams`)"
    application:
      - "`AuditEnvelopeFactoryImpl::with_pinned_inputs`, `RecoveryContext`, `classify`, `LlmBudgetReservation`"
    infrastructure:
      - ".pi/doctest-floors.tsv (raised), .pi/doctest-exemptions.tsv (new, if any exemption survives)"
    interfaces:
      - "None"

  citations:
    - file: ".pi/doctest-floors.tsv"
      note: "the rationale comment and the measured 16 / 6 / 10 line; floor `rigorix_engine 6`"
    - file: "engine/src/audit/application/envelope_factory_impl.rs"
      note: ":69 the `ignore` fence on `with_pinned_inputs`"
    - file: ".pi/scripts/run-doctests.sh"
      note: "reports discovered / executed / ignored per crate and fails below the floor"

  verification:
    - "`bash .pi/scripts/run-doctests.sh` reports an executed count above 6 and the floor matches it"
    - "`cargo test --doc -p rigorix-engine -- --list | grep -c ': test'` equals discovered, and every ignored one has a row in the exemptions file or a compiling fence"
    - "Seed: rename `with_pinned_inputs` to `with_pinned_input` → the doc example fails to compile and `run-doctests.sh` fails naming the crate; restored, it passes"
    - "A converted example that would have caught a real drift is demonstrated: the seed above is that demonstration"
    - "`grep -rc '```ignore' engine/src` drops to the exemption count"
---

# Ten examples that cannot be wrong

```
$ bash .pi/scripts/run-doctests.sh
crate              discovered executed ignored  status
rigorix_engine             16        6      10  ok
```

`ok` is correct — six ran and the floor is six. But ten examples on public APIs are marked `ignore`,
which means rustdoc skips compilation entirely. A doc example that never compiles is prose with code
formatting; it cannot fail when the API changes, which is the only thing it is for.

The zero-risk conversion is most of them: `no_run` compiles the example and skips execution, which
is exactly right for anything needing a key, a socket or a database. `ignore` should mean "this
genuinely cannot be compiled" — and then it needs a reason on record, not a bare fence.
title: 10 of rigorix_engine's 16 doctests are `ignore` — including the example for `with_pinned_inputs`, the documented way to use ADR-014's carrier — so they never compile

---
guardian_issue:
  id: "ISSUE-REPORT-CITES-SUPERSEDED-MODULE-COUNT"
  title: "The spike report still states '25 of 38 modules excluded, 11 of them for a forbidden crate'; the `--gates` check established 22 and 10, and the report's own convention is to annotate supersessions"
  epic: "portable-slice"
  component: "Docs"
  module: "wasm-seam"
  status: planned
  priority: low
  tracking_issue: 1378
  dependencies:
    - "#1374 (the `--gates` check that re-derived the counts)"
    - "the ADR-014 §1 correction (companion issue)"

  intent: |
    `docs/spike-portable-slice-2026-11.md:402` states the inventory finding it still stands behind:

    > 2. **M1's inventory stands** and is unaffected: **25 of 38** modules excluded, **11** of them for
    >    a forbidden crate.

    Both numbers are superseded. #1374's `--gates` check found that three rows claiming "whole module"
    (`dag_engine`, `event_system`, `observability`) do not compile when gated whole — they are item
    rows — so the honest counts are **22 of 38** modules and **10** for a forbidden crate. The
    manifest, ADR-014 and the ratios file all moved; the report did not.

    The report is the measurement record, and its convention — established by #1354, #1361 and
    #1357 — is that a superseded number stays visible **with the correction attached**, because the
    history of why a number moved is itself the evidence. Deleting the sentence would be wrong; it
    is still the finding M1 produced on the branch. Leaving it unannotated is also wrong: it reads as
    the current count, and it is the count the ADR no longer states.

    This matters more than a stale figure normally would, because the re-derivation is itself
    instructive: three manifest rows claiming a whole module were never gated whole until #1374's
    check tried it. That is a finding about the manifest's own claims, and the report is where a
    reader learns what the inventory cost.

  in_scope:
    - "The sentence keeps the branch-era numbers and gains the correction: 22 of 38 and 10, with the reason (three `whole module` rows were item rows, found by `--gates` in #1374) and a pointer to ADR-014 §1 and the manifest summary"
    - "The report's M1 row in the measurements table is checked for the same number and annotated if present"

  out_of_scope:
    - "Re-measuring M1. The branch figure was correct for the manifest as it existed; the correction is about what the manifest claims, not about the run"
    - "Editing the ADR or the ratios file (companion issue)"
    - "The 74-crate figure, re-measured today on the merged tree and still 74"

  affected_layers:
    domain:
      - "None"
    application:
      - "None"
    infrastructure:
      - "None"
    interfaces:
      - "None"

  citations:
    - file: "docs/spike-portable-slice-2026-11.md"
      note: ":402 the M1 inventory bullet; §0-§1's table for the M1 row"
    - file: "engine/.pi/portable-inventory.tsv"
      note: "the summary that now reads 22 of 38; `dag_engine`, `event_system`, `observability` are item rows"
    - file: "wasm/.pi/architecture/decisions/ADR-014-portable-slice-and-pinned-inputs.md"
      note: "§1, the re-derived counts"

  verification:
    - "Every stated count in the report adjacent to 'modules excluded' equals the manifest summary: `grep -n 'of 38' docs/spike-portable-slice-2026-11.md` shows 22 in any current claim, and 25 only inside an annotated supersession"
    - "The annotation names the three rows and the check that found them"
    - "A reader can reach ADR-014 §1 and the manifest from the sentence without searching"
---

# The measurement record, one manifest revision behind

The report is not wrong about what it measured. It is wrong about what the manifest says *now*, and
it says so in the section a reader goes to for the inventory's cost — which is the number every
later estimate inherits.
title: The spike report still states '25 of 38 modules excluded, 11 of them for a forbidden crate'; the `--gates` check established 22 and 10, and the report's own convention is to annotate supersessions

body:
---
guardian_issue:
  id: "ISSUE-ADR014-BARE-COUNTS-STALE-AND-UNCHECKED"
  title: "ADR-014 §1 now contradicts itself in one paragraph — '22 of 38 … Of those 25, only 11' next to '12 of 22' and '10 of 22' — because the guard checks ratio-shaped tokens and not bare counts"
  epic: "portable-slice"
  component: "Docs"
  module: "wasm-seam"
  status: planned
  priority: medium
  tracking_issue: 1377
  dependencies:
    - "#1374 (re-derived the counts; updated the tokens the guard sees)"
    - "#1363 / #1365 (the ratio and count guards)"

  intent: |
    The `--gates` check in #1374 found three false rows in the merged manifest (`dag_engine`,
    `event_system`, `observability` claimed "whole module" and gating them whole does not compile).
    The honest counts are **22 of 38** modules and **22 items**, 10 forbidden-crate + 6 narrowed
    `tokio` = 16 direct, 6 closure.

    The guarded tokens moved with them — the guard derives `22 of 38`, `12 of 22`, `10 of 22`,
    `22 items` and passes. Inside the same paragraph, two bare counts did not move:

    > Four counts are recorded here …: **74 crates** …, **22 of 38** public modules excluded, **22
    > inner items** …, and **9 dependencies** removed. **Of those 25, only 11 leave for a forbidden
    > crate**; 6 leave because they need a `tokio` feature the slice narrows away and 6 because they
    > name a symbol from an excluded module. So **12 of 22** leave for something that is *not* a
    > dependency statement, and any future "just remove `reqwest`" reasoning reaches only **10 of 22**.

    10 + 6 + 6 = 22 and 22 − 10 = 12, so the paragraph's own arithmetic is right and the two bare
    figures are wrong: there is no "25" and no "11". The ratios file carries a third copy of the
    stale pair in a provenance note — `10 of 22` is derived with the note "a description of the
    dependency list reaches **11 of the 25**".

    The guard cannot see any of them. It extracts `N of M`, `N %`, and vague quantifiers; a bare
    integer followed by a noun is not a shape it recognises, so #1374 re-derived exactly the tokens
    the guard reads and left the adjacent prose describing the previous counts.

    Verified, on a clean tree: `bash .pi/scripts/validate-portable-inventory.sh` prints
    `10 forbidden-crate + 6 narrowed-tokio = 16 direct, 6 closure · 22 of 38 modules · 22 items ·
    9 dependencies`, `22 derivation rows`, and exits 0 — with both stale numbers in the record it
    certifies.

  in_scope:
    - "ADR-014 §1's bare counts corrected: there is no 25 and no 11; the sentence reads 22 modules, of which 10 leave for a forbidden crate"
    - "The ratios file's `10 of 22` provenance note corrected to the same numbers"
    - "The guard extended to bare counts: any integer in the record immediately followed by one of the derived count nouns (modules, items, dependencies, crates) must equal the derived value for that noun, and a count noun with a subject the guard cannot derive is a failure with a reason — the same rule #1363 applied to ratios"
    - "Seeds: `Of those 25` → exit 1 naming the line and both values; `only 11 leave` → exit 1"

  out_of_scope:
    - "Re-deriving the counts again. 10 + 6 + 6 = 22 and 22 − 10 = 12 are confirmed against the manifest and the guard's own summary"
    - "The report's copy of the superseded count — filed separately, because it is the measurement record rather than the decision record"
    - "`74 crates`: measured again today on the merged tree (`cargo tree -p rigorix-engine --features portable --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -e normal,build` → 74 unique), so it is correct, not merely unchecked"

  affected_layers:
    domain:
      - "None"
    application:
      - "None"
    infrastructure:
      - ".pi/scripts/validate-portable-inventory.sh — the bare-count rule"
      - "wasm/.pi/adr-014-ratios.tsv — one provenance note"
    interfaces:
      - "None"

  citations:
    - file: "wasm/.pi/architecture/decisions/ADR-014-portable-slice-and-pinned-inputs.md"
      note: "§1, the paragraph beginning 'Four counts are recorded here'"
    - file: "wasm/.pi/adr-014-ratios.tsv"
      note: "the `count 10 of 22 excluded_crate …` row's provenance cell"
    - file: ".pi/scripts/validate-portable-inventory.sh"
      note: "the ratio extraction; its summary line prints the derived counts"

  verification:
    - "`bash .pi/scripts/validate-portable-inventory.sh` exits 0 and the ADR paragraph contains no integer contradicting its summary line"
    - "Seed: replace `22 of 38 public modules excluded` with `22 modules excluded` in the prose → the guard exits 1, naming the line and the subject it cannot derive"
    - "Seed: set `Of those 25` → `Of those 21` → exit 1 (21 ≠ 22); restored, exit 0"
    - "Seed: set `only 11 leave` → `only 10 leave` → exit 0, because 10 is right; then `only 10` → `only 12` → exit 1"
    - "`--self-test` gains the bare-count cases and reports more than 14 assertions"
---

# The paragraph the guard protects, disagreeing with itself

```
ADR-014 §1:  **22 of 38** modules   …   Of those 25, only 11 leave for a forbidden crate   …
             6 … 6 …   So 12 of 22   …   reaches only 10 of 22
```

A reader gets four different module totals from one paragraph: 22, 25, 12-of-22, 10-of-22. Three of
them are consistent; the fourth — "those 25" and "only 11" — is the count from before #1374.

This is the same class as #1363 one level down. There, the guard read one of ten ratio statements;
here, it reads every ratio-shaped token and none of the bare ones. The fix is the same shape of
rule, not a bigger regex: **a count noun with a number the guard cannot derive is a failure**, so a
re-derivation either updates the prose or fails the build.
title: ADR-014 §1 now contradicts itself in one paragraph — '22 of 38 … Of those 25, only 11' next to '12 of 22' and '10 of 22' — because the guard checks ratio-shaped tokens and not bare counts
